title: Elsa Schiaparelli's birth chart
metaDescription: Elsa Schiaparelli's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 17.7° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Venus and Jupiter sit 0.7° from an exact square — near enough that the tradition reads taste and expansion as a single working part. Nothing in a square flows; everything in it works. The old texts kept squares for the charts they respected.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Virgo, but precisely: 17.7°, second decan, 10°–20°, under Saturn in the triplicity scheme. The tradition kept these divisions because thirty degrees is a long street.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Mercury holds 13.4° Libra, Venus holds 3.6° Scorpio, Mars holds 21.9° Sagittarius — in the old shorthand, a mind at home in argument and pattern; taste tuned to mood and undertow; drive that ignites on contact.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The day's firmest angle joins Venus and Jupiter — a square holding at 0.7°. A square is the tradition’s engine room: two drives at cross purposes, and the friction is the horsepower. Behind it, Saturn square Pluto at 0.8°, and Neptune conjunction Pluto at 1.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon opposes Jupiter while both square Venus. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has one entry for this chart. Venus in Scorpio at 3.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: The certain ground: 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, dividing 5 air, 2 earth, 1 water, 1 fire by element and 5 mutable, 2 cardinal, 2 fixed by mode. Jupiter, Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Cancer into Leo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 11.8° between one midnight and the next. A birth time would settle it in a second; there isn’t one. So the Moon stays unnamed here — the alternative is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact.
